summary.oneLiner: A Mumbai-based, four-decade-old manufacturer and exporter of studded jewellery and cut & polished diamonds now expanding into domestic jewellery manufacturing and lab-grown diamonds.
summary.business: Golkunda Diamonds & Jewellery Limited manufactures studded jewellery and deals in cut & polished diamonds, precious and semi-precious stones, primarily for export to long-standing retail-chain customers in Europe and the Middle East. It is now setting up a domestic manufacturing facility to supply fine jewellery to organised retail chains across major Indian cities.

risks.note: The United States is one of the largest export destinations for India's gems & jewellery industry; any increase in US import duties, tariff barriers or bilateral trade policy changes may hurt export competitiveness, pricing and volumes.

Escalating US-Iran-Israel tensions and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war may raise gold price volatility, logistics/freight costs, disrupt shipping routes and cause forex fluctuations, impacting global trade and business sentiment.
Fluctuations in gold, diamond and other precious metal prices can impact input costs and operating margins.
As an export-oriented business, foreign exchange rate fluctuations could affect export realisations and overall profitability.

Business is significantly oriented toward exports (to Europe, Middle East and the US); dependence on export markets is a structural concentration the Company is now seeking to reduce via domestic expansion.
Intensifying competition from domestic and international jewellery manufacturers may lead to pricing and margin pressures.
Changes in consumer spending patterns for luxury products, and discretionary spending pressure from gold price fluctuations and economic uncertainty, can affect demand.

Board-level risk management identifies raw material price risk, financial risk and foreign currency risk as key risks monitored on a continuing basis, though none currently viewed as threatening the Company's existence.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for branded jewellery, diamond jewellery and premium lifestyle products remained comparatively resilient despite gold price fluctuations and broader economic uncertainty.
- Growing domestic demand for jewellery supported by rising disposable incomes, rapid urbanisation and evolving consumer preferences.
- Global jewellery market growth expected to continue, supported by rising consumer spending, wider acceptance of lab-grown diamonds and rapid expansion of digital retail platforms, with sustained demand from Asia and the Middle East.
- India expected to remain among the fastest-growing major economies in FY2026-27, with GDP growth projected to exceed 6%, supporting continued expansion of organised retail and jewellery consumption.
- Potential Free Trade Agreements and bilateral trade arrangements with major developed economies expected to enhance export competitiveness and open new growth avenues.
- Increasing consumer preference for branded, premium and value-added jewellery creating opportunities for product diversification.
- Threats to the outlook include volatility in gold, diamond and precious metal prices, foreign exchange fluctuations, tariff barriers/protectionist policies, and intensifying domestic and international competition.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Diversify revenue base by expanding into the domestic Indian jewellery market via a new manufacturing facility at Andheri, Mumbai, reducing dependence on export markets.
- Continue to strengthen the core export business while building domestic market presence during the coming financial year.
- Strengthen position in the lab-grown diamond segment with premium-quality jewellery.
- Explore strategic partnerships, alliances and acquisition opportunities to accelerate entry into the B2C retail business.
- Expand product portfolio, strengthen customer engagement and improve operational efficiencies.
- Company declares dividends subject to shareholder approval; declaration of the final dividend for FY2025-26 was placed as an ordinary business item for approval at the 36th AGM (20th August 2026). No further stated policy on buyback, debt reduction or reinvestment intent is disclosed in this bundle.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has established a new manufacturing facility at Andheri, Mumbai to strengthen its presence in the domestic jewellery market, leveraging over four decades of manufacturing and export experience. The facility will manufacture and supply a comprehensive range of fine jewellery — diamond, gold, gemstone, jadau and lab-grown diamond jewellery — to leading retail chains and organised jewellery retailers across major Indian cities. Establishment and scale-up of the facility is being funded in part through a preferential allotment of convertible warrants, and is intended to diversify the Company's revenue base and reduce dependence on export markets. No commissioning date, capacity figure or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this bundle.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over 40 years of experience in manufacturing and exporting fine jewellery
- Strong, enduring relationships with renowned retail chains across Europe and the Middle East
- Long-standing customer relationships and a well-diversified export market presence
- Disciplined inventory management and commitment to quality, operational excellence and timely delivery

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- US tariff / trade-policy exposure — The United States is one of the largest export destinations for India's gems & jewellery industry; any increase in US import duties, tariff barriers or bilateral trade policy changes may hurt export competitiveness, pricing and volumes.
- Geopolitical conflict exposure — Escalating US-Iran-Israel tensions and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war may raise gold price volatility, logistics/freight costs, disrupt shipping routes and cause forex fluctuations, impacting global trade and business sentiment.
- Gold and diamond price volatility — Fluctuations in gold, diamond and other precious metal prices can impact input costs and operating margins.
- Foreign exchange rate risk — As an export-oriented business, foreign exchange rate fluctuations could affect export realisations and overall profitability.
- Export market concentration — Business is significantly oriented toward exports (to Europe, Middle East and the US); dependence on export markets is a structural concentration the Company is now seeking to reduce via domestic expansion.
- Competitive intensity — Intensifying competition from domestic and international jewellery manufacturers may lead to pricing and margin pressures.
- Discretionary/luxury demand sensitivity — Changes in consumer spending patterns for luxury products, and discretionary spending pressure from gold price fluctuations and economic uncertainty, can affect demand.
- Raw material and financial risk — Board-level risk management identifies raw material price risk, financial risk and foreign currency risk as key risks monitored on a continuing basis, though none currently viewed as threatening the Company's existence.
